page_texts.4:
[patterns/application/api-microservices/PTN-APP-API-040-design-first-seam-contract-pattern.md#problem-statement]

### Problem Statement

Behavioral decomposition builds *nodes* (capabilities) but is blind to *edges* — the contracts joining components. An edge has no behavioral scenario of its own, so it produces no work item and each adjacent node's tests pass with the other side stubbed. The edge is therefore built by no one and discovered missing (or drifted) only at integration.
page_texts.5:
[patterns/application/api-microservices/PTN-APP-API-040-design-first-seam-contract-pattern.md#solution-overview]

### Solution Overview

Promote every cross-component **seam** to a first-class, **design-first contract** authored in the native industry standard for its class — OpenAPI 3.1 (sync-api), AsyncAPI 3.0 (event), OPA/Rego (cross-cutting policy) — with producer/consumer accountability, an owning work item, and a merge-blocking cohesion gate. Both sides bind to the one contract; the producer is generated-from/verified-against it and the consumer builds to it.
page_texts.6:
[patterns/application/api-microservices/PTN-APP-API-040-design-first-seam-contract-pattern.md#when-to-use]

### When to Use

- Any interface between independently-built components, teams, or **isolated AI agents**.
- Whenever a capability fans out into layers/services that must integrate (UI↔API, service↔service, publisher↔subscriber, feature↔policy).
page_texts.7:
[patterns/application/api-microservices/PTN-APP-API-040-design-first-seam-contract-pattern.md#benefits]

### Benefits

- Eliminates the "built by no one" seam failure by giving every edge an owner and a gate.
- Enables safe parallel/agentic delivery — isolated builders converge on one contract instead of drifting.
- Uses formats reviewers already know (low onboarding); no bespoke DSL.
page_texts.9:
[patterns/application/api-microservices/PTN-APP-API-040-design-first-seam-contract-pattern.md#business-context]

### Business Context

Delivery is decomposed across teams and, increasingly, autonomous agents. The value at risk is integration correctness: a claims platform where the UI ships against a stubbed API, an event with no consumer, or a route with no authorization check is not merely incomplete — it is a production and compliance hazard.
page_texts.10:
[patterns/application/api-microservices/PTN-APP-API-040-design-first-seam-contract-pattern.md#technical-context]

### Technical Context

Spec-driven pipelines emit work from behavioral specs (Gherkin). Those specify observable behavior at a single boundary — not the boundary itself. Microservice, event-driven, and BFF architectures are *mostly edges*; a decomposition blind to edges is blind to most of the system's integration surface.
page_texts.11:
[patterns/application/api-microservices/PTN-APP-API-040-design-first-seam-contract-pattern.md#problem-details]

### Problem Details

Concretely: a UI team and API team each "finish" against mutual stubs and the screen renders no live data; a service publishes an event no one subscribes to; an endpoint serves PHI with no policy decision because the authorization edge was never a work item. Each is the same shape — *no scenario → no artifact → no owner → no gate → built by no one*.
page_texts.12:
[patterns/application/api-microservices/PTN-APP-API-040-design-first-seam-contract-pattern.md#forces-and-constraints]

### Forces and Constraints

- **Isolation vs convergence** — isolated builders (teams/agents) cannot converge on an unspecified interface emergently.
- **Onboarding vs bespoke power** — a custom contract format is expensive to learn; recognized standards are cheap.
- **Design cost vs escape cost** — up-front contract authoring costs effort but is far cheaper than late integration failure.
page_texts.14:
[patterns/application/api-microservices/PTN-APP-API-040-design-first-seam-contract-pattern.md#pattern-description]

### Pattern Description

For each seam, author a **design-time contract** in the native standard for its class, before implementation, as an owned artifact both sides bind to. Classify the seam, author the contract, declare producer/consumer accountability, reference shared shapes canonically, and enforce a cohesion gate that fails the build unless the producer is served and the consumer is wired.
page_texts.15:
[patterns/application/api-microservices/PTN-APP-API-040-design-first-seam-contract-pattern.md#architecture-diagram]

### Architecture Diagram

```
        design time                          build time                      gate
  ┌───────────────────┐            ┌───────────────────────┐        ┌────────────────────┐
  │  Seam Contract     │  binds     │ Producer  ── served ──│        │ arch-health-check   │
  │  (OpenAPI/AsyncAPI │◄──────────►│                        │───────►│ Phase 11 cohesion   │
  │   /OPA-Rego)       │  binds     │ Consumer  ── wired  ──│        │ (served AND wired)  │
  │  x-producer /       │◄──────────►│                        │        │ else FAIL           │
  │  x-consumers        │            └───────────────────────┘        └────────────────────┘
  └───────────────────┘
        owned work item per side; shared shapes $ref _components/
```
page_texts.16:
[patterns/application/api-microservices/PTN-APP-API-040-design-first-seam-contract-pattern.md#components]

### Components

| Component | Responsibility | Dependencies |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Seam Contract | the single design-time artifact both sides bind to | native standard (OpenAPI/AsyncAPI/Rego); `_components/` for shared shapes |
| Producer work item | build the served producer generated-from/verified-against the contract | the contract |
| Consumer work item | build the consumer bound to the contract | the contract |
| Cohesion gate | fail the build unless producer served AND consumer wired | `/eap-sdd-health-check` Phase 11 |
page_texts.17:
[patterns/application/api-microservices/PTN-APP-API-040-design-first-seam-contract-pattern.md#interactions]

### Interactions

The contract is authored in logical architecture (integration phase). Export halts if a declared seam has no resolving contract. The producer and consumer are dispatched as separate owned work items, each pointing at the contract. At merge, the cohesion gate verifies both ends. Post-go-live changes propagate forward-only (a new superseding version; existing consumers not silently broken).
page_texts.18:
[patterns/application/api-microservices/PTN-APP-API-040-design-first-seam-contract-pattern.md#variations]

### Variations

| Seam class | Native standard | Governing standard |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **sync-api** (request/response) | OpenAPI 3.1 | STD-APP-API-001 |
| **event** (publish/subscribe) | AsyncAPI 3.0 | STD-APP-EVT-008 |
| **cross-cutting** (authz/policy) | OPA/Rego | GUID-SEC-IMPL-002 (+ STD-GOV-QA-002 for the invariant) |
| **journey** (cross-BC path) | Arazzo | (composes existing seam operations) |

Shared data shapes across classes are canonical per STD-INF-DM-001.
page_texts.20:
[patterns/application/api-microservices/PTN-APP-API-040-design-first-seam-contract-pattern.md#prerequisites]

### Prerequisites

- A logical architecture that identifies the seams (integration phase).
- The native-standard tooling for the relevant class.
- The canonical `_components/` library for shared shapes (STD-INF-DM-001).
page_texts.22:
[patterns/application/api-microservices/PTN-APP-API-040-design-first-seam-contract-pattern.md#phase-1-author]

#### Phase 1: Author

1. Classify each seam (sync-api / event / cross-cutting / journey).
2. Author the contract in the class's native standard, before implementation.
3. Declare producer/consumer accountability (`x-producer`/`x-consumers`); `$ref` shared shapes from `_components/`.
page_texts.23:
[patterns/application/api-microservices/PTN-APP-API-040-design-first-seam-contract-pattern.md#phase-2-build-and-gate]

#### Phase 2: Build and gate

1. Dispatch producer and consumer as separate owned work items, each bound to the contract.
2. Generate/verify the producer against the contract; bind the consumer to it.
3. Enforce the cohesion gate (producer served AND consumer wired) at merge.
page_texts.25:
[patterns/application/api-microservices/PTN-APP-API-040-design-first-seam-contract-pattern.md#example-uiapi-sync-seam-binding]

#### Example: UI↔API sync seam binding

```yaml
# UI data binding references a design-time OpenAPI operation (contractRef),
# not an invented shape:
contractRef: 'docs/design/seam-contracts/sync-api/claims/openapi.json#/paths/~1claims~1{id}/get'
producingService: 'claims-bff -> claims-api'
dependencyTier: T2   # buildable against the contract; DONE when producer serves conformant data
```
page_texts.26:
[patterns/application/api-microservices/PTN-APP-API-040-design-first-seam-contract-pattern.md#best-practices]

### Best Practices

- Author the contract before dispatching either side; never let one side invent the shape.
- Treat a permanent stub as a failure — a T2 binding is done only when its producer serves contract-conformant data.
- Keep producer/consumer identity on the contract so accountability is explicit.
page_texts.27:
[patterns/application/api-microservices/PTN-APP-API-040-design-first-seam-contract-pattern.md#common-pitfalls]

### Common Pitfalls

- **Bespoke wrapper** — inventing a custom contract format instead of the native standard (high onboarding cost; avoid).
- **Orphaned edge** — a produced event/endpoint with no declared consumer (a defect, not a deferral).
- **Inlined shared shape** — copying a cross-context shape instead of `$ref`ing `_components/` (re-opens drift).

page_texts.30:
[patterns/application/api-microservices/PTN-APP-API-040-design-first-seam-contract-pattern.md#compliance-requirements]

### Compliance Requirements

Cross-cutting (authorization) seams carry compliance weight (HIPAA); their policy is authored by design and verified independently (see GUID-SEC-IMPL-002 and STD-GOV-QA-002 for the invariant side).
page_texts.31:
[patterns/application/api-microservices/PTN-APP-API-040-design-first-seam-contract-pattern.md#approval-process]

### Approval Process

Seam contracts are approved in logical architecture review before the producing/consuming work items are dispatched.
page_texts.32:
[patterns/application/api-microservices/PTN-APP-API-040-design-first-seam-contract-pattern.md#monitoring-and-metrics]

### Monitoring and Metrics

| Metric | Target | Measurement Method |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Seams with a design-time contract | 100% | `/eap-decom-spec-export-issues` halt on unresolved seam |
| Seam cohesion (served + wired) | 100% | `/eap-sdd-health-check` Phase 11 |
| Orphaned edges | 0 | Phase 11 |
page_texts.34:
[patterns/application/api-microservices/PTN-APP-API-040-design-first-seam-contract-pattern.md#real-world-example-1]

### Real-World Example 1

**Context:** UI shipped against a stubbed BFF whose backend was never built.
**Implementation:** the UI data binding was required to `contractRef` a design-time OpenAPI operation; the backend `[api]` producer became an owned work item; the cohesion gate failed until the producer served conformant data.
**Outcome:** the "screens built, providers missing" failure was caught at design/merge time.
page_texts.35:
[patterns/application/api-microservices/PTN-APP-API-040-design-first-seam-contract-pattern.md#real-world-example-2]

### Real-World Example 2

**Context:** An event published with no subscriber.
**Implementation:** the AsyncAPI contract required `x-consumers`; Phase 11 failed the orphaned channel.
**Outcome:** the edge got an owner or was removed — not silently shipped.
page_texts.37:
[patterns/application/api-microservices/PTN-APP-API-040-design-first-seam-contract-pattern.md#scenario-1-two-agents-one-seam]

#### Scenario 1: Two agents, one seam

Two isolated agents build a producer and consumer independently; both bind to the one contract, so they converge without communication.
page_texts.38:
[patterns/application/api-microservices/PTN-APP-API-040-design-first-seam-contract-pattern.md#scenario-2-post-go-live-change]

#### Scenario 2: Post-go-live change

A change to a shipped seam emits a new superseding contract version; existing consumers migrate deliberately — the shipped work item is never silently mutated.
page_texts.40:
[patterns/application/api-microservices/PTN-APP-API-040-design-first-seam-contract-pattern.md#before-problem-state]

#### Before (Problem State)

Edges implicit; each node tested against stubs; integration failures found in production.
page_texts.41:
[patterns/application/api-microservices/PTN-APP-API-040-design-first-seam-contract-pattern.md#after-solution-state]

#### After (Solution State)

Every edge is a design-first contract with an owner and a cohesion gate; integration correctness is provable before merge.

[patterns/application/api-microservices/PTN-APP-API-040-design-first-seam-contract-pattern.md#tldr]

## TL;DR

**Problem:** Behavioral decomposition builds nodes, not edges — an unowned seam is built by no one and fails at integration.

**Solution:** Author every cross-component seam as a design-first contract in its native standard (OpenAPI/AsyncAPI/Rego), with producer/consumer accountability, an owning work item, and a served-AND-wired cohesion gate.

**When to Use:** Any interface between independently-built components, teams, or isolated AI agents.

**Key Benefits:**
- Eliminates the "built by no one" seam failure
- Enables safe parallel/agentic delivery via one shared contract
- Uses recognized standards — low onboarding, no bespoke DSL

**Implementation Complexity:** Medium

**Prerequisites:** Logical architecture identifying seams; native-standard tooling; canonical `_components/` library.

**Related Patterns:** PTN-APP-API-001 (BFF), PTN-APP-API-015 (OpenAPI), PTN-APP-API-035 (Contract Testing).
